did_you_know.text: Psalm 136 opens with a call to give thanks to the Lord for His goodness, immediately adding the refrain repeated throughout the psalm: “For His steadfast love endures forever.”
The verse describes the Lord as the One who alone performs “great wonders,” meaning that the great deeds are attributed to Him alone.
In this verse, creation is described as making the heavens “with understanding,” not merely as an act of power.
The psalm calls the sun, moon, and stars “great lights,” and continues by describing their roles in governing the day and night.
At this point, the psalm moves from describing creation to recounting events in Israel’s history, beginning with the plague of the firstborn in Egypt.
The splitting of the Red Sea is described with the phrase “divided into parts,” emphasizing the sea’s division into passages.
After describing the exodus from Egypt and the crossing of the sea, the verse also recalls the Lord’s guidance of Israel in the wilderness.
The psalm names Sihon, king of the Amorites, as one of the kings whom the Lord struck down.
The verse presents the result of the victory over the kings: giving their land “as an inheritance.”
The final verse sums up the psalm with a call to give thanks “to the God of heaven,” repeating once more that His steadfast love endures forever.
